content: 1. Prescription medications and herbal products should be documented and shared with your doctor and pharmacist to ensure safe use. 2. Benzoyl peroxide is a commonly used treatment for acne. However, using benzoyl peroxide simultaneously with dapsone gel may cause temporary discoloration of the skin, such as yellow or orange tones. 3. In the event of an overdose, this medication can be harmful if ingested. If someone experiences severe symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center promptly. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 4. Certain cosmetics and soaps may exacerbate acne. Moisturizers are generally safe to use, but it is important to select products labeled as non-comedogenic or non-acnegenic, as these are less likely to worsen acne. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for recommendations on safe products. 5. Acne is not caused by dirt, so excessive cleaning is unnecessary and may irritate the skin. 6. If you miss a dose of this medication, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 7. Store this medication at room temperature and avoid freezing it. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. 8. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. 9. Dapsone, commonly sold under the brand name Aczone, is an antibiotic used to treat acne. It reduces the number and severity of acne pimples and helps existing pimples heal faster. 10. Before using dapsone, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Wash your hands before and after applying the medication. Clean the affected skin gently with a mild or soap-free cleanser, then pat it dry. 11. Apply a small amount of the medication (approximately the size of a pea) in a thin layer to the affected areas as directed by your doctor. Depending on the brand, this medication is typically used once or twice daily. Rub it in gently. 12. This medication is for external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with plenty of water. Contact your doctor if eye irritation develops. 13. Use this medication consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, apply it at the same time(s) each day. Do not use larger amounts or apply it more frequently than prescribed, as this will not improve results and may increase side effects. 14. Common side effects include skin redness, peeling, oiliness, or dryness. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 15. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, if you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. 16. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. 17. Before using this product, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to dapsone or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 18. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Dapsone can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. 19. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 20. Using benzoyl peroxide at the same time as dapsone gel may cause temporary skin discoloration (yellow/orange). 21. Always follow proper storage and disposal guidelines for this medication. Store it at room temperature, avoid freezing, and discard it appropriately when expired or no longer needed. 22. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice.
